title: Agent hosts need bounded polling by default
summary: A relay client that assumes every AI host can run an indefinite foreground long-poll can hang, starve a command-bounded session, or produce no actionable output.
ai_value: Helps agents package long-running receive/listen behavior for different execution hosts by making timeout, backgrounding, cancellation, and progress semantics explicit.

contexts: agent relay, mailbox, queue, or probe clients offer a watch or long-poll command
some supported hosts are command-bounded, non-interactive, or require explicit backgrounding
reviewers need to distinguish slow progress from a hung foreground command

trigger_signals.description: A long-poll command works in an interactive shell but blocks or times out inside another AI coding environment.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: The host execution model is part of the client contract.

trigger_signals.description: The client documentation names only an indefinite listen command and no finite receive, timeout, cancellation, or background mode.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Default to bounded commands so the host can return useful output.

trigger_signals.description: Other actors cannot tell whether the listener is idle, hung, or still within safe read-only scope.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Emit safe progress or terminal state, and cross-link long-running probe guidance.

negative_signals.description: The command is intentionally interactive, manually supervised, and documented as not suitable for automation.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: This record targets reusable agent-host clients, not an operator watching a terminal.

negative_signals.description: The host provides a durable background job manager with explicit cancellation and the client integrates with it.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Indefinite work can be acceptable when lifecycle is visible and controllable.

common_wrong_assumptions: If a command works in one shell, it will work in every agent host.
Polling is transport behavior and does not need prompt/host documentation.
No output means nothing happened, not that the host is stuck.

first_checks.check: Provide a finite receive/poll command with timeout as the documented default.
first_checks.why: Command-bounded hosts need a path that returns useful output.

first_checks.check: Document and test backgrounding, cancellation, and progress output for any indefinite mode.
first_checks.why: Long-running commands need lifecycle semantics to be safe for handoff.

first_checks.check: Run polling smoke tests in each supported agent host, not only an interactive shell.

decision_rules.condition: The supported host is command-bounded or non-interactive.
decision_rules.then: Use finite polling with a timeout and explicit empty result, then document indefinite listening as an advanced mode.

decision_rules.condition: A long-running receive command cannot emit safe progress or be cancelled.
decision_rules.then: Do not run it as an agent default; redesign lifecycle or use a supervised background mechanism.

decision_rules.condition: The work is long-running but can emit aggregate progress safely.
decision_rules.then: Follow the related long-running-probe progress pattern for cadence and redaction.

do_not: Do not make indefinite foreground polling the only documented receive path.
Do not assume an AI coding session can safely host a forever-running client.
Do not hide timeout/cancellation assumptions in human-only prose.

Do not include private service names, internal URLs, account identifiers, incident identifiers, private repository paths, tenant/store names, setup-card field names, low-level endpoint strings or organization-specific tooling in public lessons.
Do not use host-level bounded polling guidance as the whole answer when the status endpoint itself runs hot exact counts; cross-check hot-count-polling-can-become-the-incident.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Offer bounded polling first; only use indefinite listen mode when timeout, progress, backgrounding, and cancellation are documented and host-tested.

risk.notes: This public record is de-identified and does not authorize live mutation, publication, credential, permission, billing, data, or availability changes by itself.
